overview.title: The candidate
overview.text: NWPT-SM32300, an investigational 300 mg oral softgel of highly purified cannabidiol in a self-emulsifying (micellar) lipid formulation. It is not approved for any use.

overview.title: Completed
overview.text: A Phase 1 study in 14 healthy volunteers, completed on 10 December 2025. Its results have not yet been published.

overview.title: In progress
overview.text: Finalisation of the Phase 2B protocol, reported as in progress on 23 February 2026. No completion date has been announced.

overview.title: Not yet known
overview.text: Whether NWPT-SM32300 helps people at clinical high risk of psychosis. Finding out is the purpose of the research.

stages.title: Why people at clinical high risk are a research priority
stages.asks: What is known about people who meet criteria for clinical high risk of psychosis (CHR-P), and what care is recommended today.
points: CHR-P is not a diagnosis of psychosis or schizophrenia, and most people in this group do not develop psychosis.
An updated meta-analysis estimated that about one in four people identified as CHR-P (pooled estimate, 25%) developed psychosis within three years.
In England, psychological therapy is the recommended first step. NICE advises against antipsychotics to prevent psychosis in this group.
No preventive intervention has been shown to work better than the others.

stages.title: An oral softgel designed for a poorly water-soluble medicine
stages.asks: Whether a fixed-strength micellar softgel is a suitable way to give cannabidiol by mouth.
points: Cannabidiol dissolves poorly in water. Taken by mouth while fasting, only about 6% of a dose is estimated to reach the bloodstream, and food changes absorption markedly (research on other CBD products).
NWPT-SM32300 is a 300 mg softgel whose contents are designed to disperse into very small droplets in the gut.
The final formulation and GMP clinical supply were completed before Phase 1 dosing in 2025.
stages.open: Whether this formulation gives more consistent absorption than other CBD products has not been published.
where: Background: established (other CBD products). NWPT-SM32300 details: programme information from company records, not published

stages.title: Phase 1 in healthy volunteers: absorption and short-term tolerability
stages.asks: How the body absorbs and handles NWPT-SM32300 after single doses, and short-term tolerability, compared with a licensed cannabidiol oral solution. It was not a study of whether NWPT-SM32300 works.
points: 14 healthy adult volunteers; randomised, open-label, three-period crossover.
Sponsor of the Phase 1 study: NWPharmaTech Ltd (as registered).
Results have not yet been published.

stages.title: The planned Phase 2B study in people at clinical high risk
stages.asks: Dose response, symptoms, safety and tolerability of NWPT-SM32300 in people at clinical high risk of psychosis, to inform the next stage of development.
points: Applicable approvals are not confirmed in public materials. Study initiation remains subject to funding, finalisation and approvals.
Oversight arrangements for the Phase 2B study have not yet been published.
A larger UK trial of cannabidiol in this group (CANTOP-RCT) was funded but never started, which is one reason this question remains open.

stages.title: Could psychosis be delayed or prevented?
stages.asks: Whether transition to psychosis can be delayed or prevented. This is a longer-term question, not the current primary aim.
points: Answering it would need an adequately powered trial with long follow-up, if it were pursued as a primary objective.
Positive results on symptoms would not, by themselves, show prevention.

Science — what is known and what remains open
sources.limit: Summarises the questions; not a result.

open_questions: Does NWPT-SM32300 reduce symptoms in people at clinical high risk?
Not established. It would take the results of a pre-specified clinical study such as the planned Phase 2B.
Is there a dose response, and which dose would be best?
Not established. Dose response is one of the planned study’s aims.
Is it safe and well tolerated in this population?
Not established. Phase 1 involved healthy volunteers and single doses only.
Does the formulation give more consistent absorption than other CBD products?
Not published. Phase 1 measured absorption; its results are awaited.
Can transition to psychosis be delayed or prevented?
A longer-term question needing a separately powered trial with long follow-up.
